summary: Chiew Hui Ho works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at Stanford University (2004–2013) and served as Discipline Chair at the University of Sydney in 2013.

Chih-fu Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He served as Director at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007) and later became its honorary director, retiring in December 2006.

Chih-mien Adrian Tseng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn, also studying with Nobuyoshi Yamabe and Canshan Cheng, and held faculty positions at Fo Guang University.

Chihiro Nakayashiki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific and Kyoto universities, with research at Himachal Pradesh, Nakayashiki held JSPS fellowships and posts at Kyoto University, Kansai University, and the University of Edinburgh.

Chijo Akamatsu was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto. He held professorships at Koyasan, Hanazono, Keijo Imperial (1927–1941), Ryukoku (1943–1947), and Yamaguchi universities.
Chijun Hamada is a scholar in Buddhist studies who was attested in 1978 as an assistant at Taisho University and as a researcher at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a master's degree from the University of British Columbia, supervised by Karin Preisendanz and Ashok Aklujkar, and completed a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura.
Chiko Corona is a practitioner and scholar of Buddhist studies who received traditional training under Kenkō Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.
Chikyo Yamamoto was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Koyasan University, serving as a professor (attested 1970) and as a part-time lecturer (attested 1980).
Chime Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar and worked at the British Library from circa 1965 to 1985.

Chin Kung was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Thomé H. Fang, Bingnan Li, and Lobsang Palden Tenpe Dronme. He taught at Chinese Culture University and founded the Corporate Body of the Buddha Educational Foundation.

Ching Keng specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, he taught at National Chengchi University and National Taiwan University.

Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Jan Nattier and completed a PhD at Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.

Chintaharan Chakravarti was an Indologist. He held posts as a professor at Presidency University, at Bethune College (attested 1941), and served as Publication Secretary at Sanskrit Sahitya Parishat (attested 1960).
Chintaman Ganesh Kashikar was an Indologist who served as Assistant Secretary at Vaidika Samshodhana Mandala (attested 1941) and as a professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
Chirapat Prapandvidya is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology. He founded Silpakorn University, served as its Director in 1996, and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

Chisan Kohō was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyodo Koshuin. He held leadership roles at Saijō-ji, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Sōji-ji, and founded Tsurumi Women's University in 1966.

Chitai Takenaka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1964–1968). He served as an associate professor at Hanazono University (1974–1988) and as a professor at Tokoha University (~1989).

Chizen Akanuma was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Kōkōdō under Manshi Kiyozawa. He taught at Otani University, co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921, and taught Keio Nishio and Genjun Sasaki.

Chizuko Yoshimizu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She earned a doctorate at the University of Vienna and has held posts at Naritasan Institute, the University of Lausanne, Toyo Bunko, and the University of Tsukuba.
